sections.h2: Where does Montcalm County keep its land records?
sections.html:
The register of deeds works out of the county building complex in Stanton, at 211 W. Main St., box 368, Stanton, MI 48888. The state Treasury directory gives 989-831-7337 as the phone line and regofdeeds@co.montcalm.mi.us as the email address. Call before you drive over, because counter hours and electronic filing options are best confirmed with the staff.

Stanton has been the seat since 1860, when county voters moved it from Greenville, the original seat dating to 1840. The city is small, with 1,348 people in the 2020 census, and it sits where four townships meet: Day, Evergreen, Sidney and Douglass. Land records for all of Montcalm County's townships end up in this one office.

sections.h2: What do Greenville and Stanton tell a seller about the market?
sections.html:
Greenville is the largest city, with 8,816 residents in 2020. It lies 16 road miles southwest of Stanton and about 33 miles northeast of Grand Rapids, which explains why Montcalm is counted in the Grand Rapids metropolitan area. The Flat River runs through town, and Baldwin, Manoka and Como lakes sit inside the city limits. Greenville built its name on refrigerator manufacturing, and it was the birthplace of the Meijer store chain. The Electrolux plant closed in 2006, a loss that affected 2,700 employees and their families.

Around the city, farms grow potatoes, corn and Christmas trees and run dairy herds. The Fred Meijer Heartland Trail ends in Greenville after 41 miles from Alma, and the Flat River Trail loops the city. A house near a lake or trail often draws a buyer who wants the recreation, so mention those features in your listing.

  • Greenville's Lafayette Street downtown district was placed on the National and State Register of Historic Places in 2008.
  • The Danish Festival fills the third weekend of August.
  • The Montcalm County 4-H Fair is held in Greenville each summer.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Montcalm County?
sections.html:
The county spans 721 square miles, of which 705 are land, and 84.6% of its people live in rural areas. The count was 66,614 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate stands at 69,406, a rise of 4.2%. Residents aged 65 and over make up 20.1% of the total.

Home ownership is high. Owners live in 83.1% of occupied housing, and the median home is valued at $185,500 for 2020 to 2024, while median gross rent is $869. Households earn $67,344 at the median, and the typical commute takes 30.7 minutes. The county issued 201 building permits in 2025.

Eight public school districts cover the county: Carson City Crystal Area, Central Montcalm, Greenville, Lakeview, Montabella, Tri County Area and Vestaburg, plus the intermediate district for Montcalm Area. Montcalm Community College is the local college.

sections.h2: What will the recording fee be in Montcalm County?
sections.html:
Under MCL 600.2567, a register collects $30.00 to enter and record one document, however many pages it runs. A single paper that assigns or discharges several instruments adds $3.00 for every one past the first. Copies are $1.00 a page, and certifying a recorded paper is $5.00.

  • Standard recording: $30.00.
  • Extra instruments in one assignment or discharge: $3.00 each.
  • Plain copies: $1.00 per page.
  • Certification: $5.00.

Payment arrives with the document, though a filing sent electronically may be paid within a business day. Only charter counties can adopt a different schedule, so verify the figures with the Stanton office before you mail a check.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax would a Montcalm County seller pay?
sections.html:
On a Montcalm sale, the grantor carries both taxes, due at the county treasurer in the 15 days after the deed is handed over. The state portion is $3.75 and the county portion $0.55 per $500 or part of $500. The table prices a sale at the county's median home value.

Family handovers get special treatment. The state act excludes a deed from a parent to a child or grandchild, and it excludes foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu. The county act has no family exclusion, so the county share can still apply. Whichever exemption fits, write it on the deed itself.

sections.h2: Which formatting rules can get a deed bounced in Stanton?
sections.html:
MCL 565.201 spells out what the register must see before accepting a paper. Missing one item means a return trip, so run a checklist with your closing agent before signing.

  • Black or dark blue signatures with each name typed or printed beneath, matching the notary's wording.
  • A grantee address on every deed, plus the drafter's name and business address.
  • A blank band of 2.5 inches across the top of page one and half an inch on all other edges.
  • A first line that names one recordable event, such as a quit claim deed.
  • Ten-point type or larger, on white paper no lighter than 20 pounds, cut between letter and legal size.
  • No more than the last four digits of a Social Security number.

Papers in a foreign language need an attached English translation. The register records whatever complies and cannot write or advise on it.

sections.h2: How does a sale change the tax bill and the homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Michigan holds yearly taxable value growth to the lesser of 5% or inflation, until ownership changes. After a transfer, taxable value jumps to the state equalized value, assessed at half of true cash value. A buyer who inherits a long-held home from a parent might avoid this, because a residential transfer to a close relative who keeps it non-commercial is excepted.

The buyer reports the change to the assessor within 45 days. The register also forwards recorded transfers to assessors every month.

A seller who claimed the principal residence exemption should file Form 2602 with the township or city assessor within 90 days after moving out. The delay penalty runs $5 per day, ending at $200, and the exemption leaves the roll at year end. A buyer moving in files Form 2368 by June 1 or November 1.

sections.h2: Can I sell an inherited or rundown Montcalm County house?
sections.html:
Yes. An heir needs authority to sign, usually through the estate's personal representative, and a certified death certificate may need to go on record if a deed names a surviving owner. The deed from the estate follows the same recording steps as any other.

A cash buyer who takes the property as it stands skips lender appraisals and repair demands, though transfer tax, recording and the assessor notice still apply. Ask the county treasurer for the parcel's tax status first, since a delinquent balance should be settled before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for a house near Greenville?
faqs.a: The Montcalm County register of deeds in Stanton, even for a Greenville address. The county has one recording office, at 211 W. Main St., and its state-listed phone number is 989-831-7337.

faqs.q: What would a seller owe in transfer tax at $185,500?
faqs.a: The total is $1,595.30, split into $1,391.25 for the state and $204.05 for the county. The seller carries it, and the price is counted in $500 blocks, rounded up.

faqs.q: Does the register of deeds supply or check my deed form?
faqs.a: The office reviews papers for recording standards and records the compliant ones. It does not draft deeds, so use an attorney or title company for the wording.

faqs.q: Will the buyer's taxes rise after the sale?
faqs.a: Usually. Ownership change lifts taxable value to the state equalized value for the next year, and the buyer reports it to the assessor within 45 days. A residential transfer to a close relative is excepted.

faqs.q: When do I give up the principal residence exemption?
faqs.a: File Form 2602 with the local assessor within 90 days of ceasing to live in the home. Filing late costs $5 per day to a $200 cap.
